overview: Trerice is a small, charming Elizabethan manor house about three miles east of Newquay, run by the National Trust since 1953. It’s a Grade I listed Tudor house with a pair of stone lions on the front lawn, and a garden with an orchard of old fruit varieties.
It’s a calmer, more intimate visit than the big stately homes, and handy if you’re staying around Newquay and want a gentle half day away from the beaches.

expect.title: The house
expect.text: Big-house grandeur in miniature, with rooms that take you from the 1500s right through to the 1950s, an enormous table and a fine collection of longcase clocks. Room guides, including Braille ones, help you get to know it.

expect.title: Garden and orchard
expect.text: A small, varied garden with an Elizabethan knot garden, cottage borders and an orchard of old fruit varieties.

expect.title: Barn café and shop
expect.text: A café in the old barn serves drinks, light bites and cake, and there’s a shop with books, gifts and local produce.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry for non-members, with family tickets; National Trust members get in free.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: There’s Blue Badge parking and accessible toilets, but some routes are steep or gravelly and access inside the house is limited to parts of the ground and first floor. A map of the accessible route is available.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: At Kestle Mill, about three miles east of Newquay.

week.text: A gentle half day close to Newquay, nice on a dry day or a showery one. Pair it with Lappa Valley next door if you have younger children.

pairWith.why: a family park with trains, just down the road

tips: Children can borrow ear defenders from reception if they need them.

setting.note: A Tudor house plus garden and orchard
